trust_mercy.title: The Reluctant Servant, Made Willing
trust_mercy.text: Jonah obeyed, and in the end, his heart caught up to his obedience. He grieved for the plant, but he understood — if only for a moment — why God grieved for Nineveh.

trust_justice.title: The Obedient Prophet, Still Unmoved
trust_justice.text: Jonah did everything asked of him. He preached, the city turned, and still he sat outside the walls, arms crossed, believing mercy was a kind of injustice. Obedience without love is its own kind of exile.

fear_mercy.title: The Fugitive Who Learned Compassion
fear_mercy.text: He ran the whole way. He resented the mission the whole way. And yet somewhere in the belly of the fish, in the wilting of a plant, compassion found him anyway — despite himself.

fear_justice.title: The Prophet Who Never Stopped Running
fear_justice.text: Even standing in Nineveh's gates, some part of Jonah was still on the road to Tarshish. He said the words God gave him, but never let them past his own heart.

conflicted.title: The Man Wrestling Both Ways
conflicted.text: Jonah's story doesn't resolve neatly, and maybe yours shouldn't either. He was afraid and faithful, angry and compassionate, all at once — closer to the real thing than any tidy ending.
